$comment: Status + body → what the SDK must do. This table is the transport, and getting one row wrong is a data-loss bug: treating 503 as success drops a batch the server never stored. Actions: drop (durably queued, forget it) | retry (keep, back off) | split (halve and resend) | hold (pause these categories) | shutdown (stop sending entirely) | degrade (change a setting, retry once).

$notes.categories: Inferred from the endpoint, never parsed from a header: /v1/batch is ['event','identify'], /v1/errors is ['error']. The server hardcodes exactly this.
$notes.headers: Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Categories are exposed cross-origin. Backoff must still work on a local schedule when they are absent, and use them when present: Retry-After sets the wait, X-RateLimit-Categories narrows which categories are held.
$notes.bodyShapes: Two 400s come from the pre-controller listener and use {"message": ...}; everything else uses {"error": ...}. Read `error ?? message`.

cases.name: accepted and durable
cases.why: 202 means durably queued in ClickHouse, not merely received. Committing the client report here is safe.

cases.name: accepted with per-event rejections
cases.why: A bad event never fails the batch. Log it in debug mode; do not resend, the server will reject it identically.

cases.name: accepted with traits dropped
cases.why: The identity link landed; only the named trait did not. Warn, do not retry.

cases.name: identify ignored
cases.why: The entry carried nothing to do. Surface it; retrying will be ignored identically. Note the codes are only what ingest can see for itself (missing_user_id, blocked_id, blocked_device_id, no_op) — a refused rebind is resolved at read time and is never reported here.

cases.name: accepted with suppressed occurrences
cases.why: Two occurrences matched the inbound filter: not stored, not billed. Surface the count; nothing to retry.

cases.name: invalid gzip
cases.why: Our compression produced something the server could not inflate. Retry once uncompressed rather than losing the batch.

cases.name: invalid JSON
cases.why: Our serializer produced junk. Retrying sends the same junk.

cases.name: bad request
cases.why: Never retry a 4xx that is not 413 or 429.

cases.name: missing key
cases.why: A config error, not a transient one. Stop sending and surface it once; continuing to buffer is a memory leak that never drains.

cases.name: batch too large by count
cases.why: Halve and resend. An SDK that respects maxItems should never see this.

cases.name: payload too large by bytes
cases.why: Split by bytes. A single item that still will not fit is dropped after shedding what it can (breadcrumbs, then source context, then frames).

cases.name: rate limited
cases.why: Hold ONLY this endpoint's categories; a throttled analytics batch must never stall an error report.

cases.name: monthly cap reached
cases.why: Retrying before the month rolls over is pure waste. Six hours, not the escalating schedule.

cases.name: storage unavailable
cases.why: THE BATCH WAS NOT STORED. An SDK that treats 503 as success loses data. The server sends Retry-After: 10.

cases.name: gateway error
cases.why: Exponential backoff with jitter, capped, then drop and record a send_error outcome.
